_: MACROARSENAL Radio : casting de la voix de Victor Sable (EN, 18/10/2026). Extrait d'essai en personnage (aucun chiffre du jour).

lines.text: Eight o'clock in Paris. Good morning, early birds, this is Victor Sable, and you're listening to MACROARSENAL Radio.
lines.tts: Eight o'clock in Paris. Good morning, early birds, this is Victor Sable, and you're listening to Macro Arsenal Radio.

lines.text: Hot coffee, screens on: let's go around the world in three minutes.
Crossing the screens: overnight, Asia opened cautiously, and the dollar is waiting for its big moment this afternoon.

From the trading floor: on the fifteenth of January, two thousand and fifteen, I was on the microphone when the Swiss National Bank scrapped its floor on the euro. Within minutes, the franc jumped more than twenty percent.
That day, I learned one thing: it's not the news that ruins a trader. It's having no plan.
The market will still be here tomorrow. So will your capital, if you protect it. This was Victor Sable. See you tomorrow, eight o'clock!

voices.label: Victor A (British baritone)
voices.design: A charismatic British male morning radio host in his early fifties with a warm, rich baritone voice, like the best presenter of a national morning news show in London. Relaxed authority, dry wit and kindness. Native British English, London, no foreign accent. Dynamic intonation that follows the meaning: lively and curious on the news, calm and serious on risk, amused and nostalgic on the trading-floor memory, warm on the goodbye, with a smile in the voice and an occasional short natural laugh. Close-microphone broadcast studio sound, natural breathing, never robotic, never monotone.

voices.label: Victor B (American, warm and bright)
voices.design: A charismatic American male morning radio host in his late forties with a warm, bright, confident voice and a natural smile, like the star host of a top business morning show in New York. Energetic, friendly and sharp. Native General American English, no foreign accent. Dynamic intonation that follows the meaning: lively and curious on the news, calm and serious on risk, amused and nostalgic on the trading-floor memory, warm on the goodbye, with a smile in the voice and an occasional short natural laugh. Close-microphone broadcast studio sound, natural breathing, never robotic, never monotone.

acting: Read it as the opening of a lively morning radio show, live on air, in English: confident, warm and smiling, natural radio rhythm with short pauses between ideas, a touch of nostalgia and humour on the trading-floor memory, and a warm, upbeat goodbye.
